tokens.name: host_session_reference
tokens.purpose: Pedagogical host id. Not sent to Auth0 or Looker.

tokens.name: host_access_token
tokens.purpose: JWT stored in browser memory. Gates /api/looker/* and /api/lab/*.

tokens.name: session_reference_token
tokens.purpose: Provides session_length param for Looker embed session identity.

tokens.name: authentication_token
tokens.purpose: Single-use /login/embed bootstrap. Stored in URL. Default Looker TTL is about 30 seconds.

tokens.name: navigation_token
tokens.purpose: In-iframe navigation JWT stored in iframe / URL. Looker TTL is about 10 minutes. Looker asks in the last 60 seconds of this token or of api_token.

tokens.name: api_token
tokens.purpose: Iframe Looker API JWT, stored in iframe. Looker TTL is about 10 minutes, on its own exp. generate_tokens rotates it together with navigation_token.

methods.where_after: Query string on GET /callback for a few seconds. Not stored.
All three stay on the HostSession. Browser never sees them. host_session_id cookie is set as the opaque handle.
Server HostSession. Rotating refresh tokens replace the stored value.
JSON body → browser memory. This is the host BFF JWT, not Auth0 access and not Looker api_token.
JSON body → browser memory. Previous host_access_token jti is dead.
JSON to browser memory. session_reference_token is stripped and stored on HostSession only.
Looker holds the real session. Host keeps session_reference_token. Browser gets the other three.

methods.method: iframe navigation to embed login URL
methods.where_after: authentication_token is consumed (dead). navigation_token stays on the embed URL as embed_navigation_token.
No tokens travel. This is a request that the host must answer with session:tokens.

Looker UI in the iframe. navigation_token is in-iframe page/dashboard navigation; api_token is iframe Looker API calls. First reply after login reuses acquire tokens; later replies need generate_tokens. Each JWT keeps its own exp.
JSON to browser, then postMessage into the iframe. Server loads session_reference_token itself — the body is not trusted as a source of session identity.
session_reference_token stays on the server and its countdown continues. New nav/api tokens go to the browser without the reference. Both siblings rotate together.
Looker session deleted. Host copy of Layer B tokens cleared. Layer A remains.
HostSession deleted. Cookie cleared. Auth0 refresh revoked when possible. Browser memory discarded.
